Vaccination is available for adults 50+ or immunocompromised individuals and is highly effective at preventing shingles and its pain.

articleSummary: Measles outbreak places Indonesia among the world’s top for vaccine-preventable diseases (PD3I) as post-pandemic transmission rebounds. Indonesia ranks around second globally for diphtheria; TB would be first per capita and second by absolute cases; leprosy ranks in the top three worldwide; hepatitis B and dengue place Indonesia first in Southeast Asia. Measles (campak) cases surged again, placing Indonesia second worldwide by late February 2026. Past spikes occurred during 2022-2023 BIAN, with success on Java and Bali but poor results elsewhere; East Java saw significant measles increases in 2025. Only one district formally declared a Local Extraordinary Event (KLB). Two Australian travelers contracted measles after visiting Indonesia, prompting official notices. The core message remains: insufficient routine immunization drives outbreak risk; mass immunization and proactive KLB responses are needed to protect public health.

articleHeadline: Novel treatment strategies for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
articleSummary: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a threat, with TB as the infectious killer. The thesis evaluates novel strategies, including repurposed drugs and drug exposure. In vitro MIC data show trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and meropenem-clavulanic acid have activity against highly drug-resistant M. tuberculosis; no clinical trials yet for TMP-SMX in MDR-TB. WHO lists meropenem-clavulanic acid as an add-on in difficult cases. A Swedish national cohort (1992–2014) of 158 MDR-TB cases links increasing MIC for fluoroquinolones to worse outcomes; older age and diabetes are risk factors, and pyrazinamide-susceptible isolates show faster culture conversion. In a prospective susceptible-TB cohort, first-line drug exposures were often subtherapeutic, with rifampicin underexposure and inter-individual variability. When MICs are considered, exposure remains low, highlighting potential value of therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM). A China cohort is planned to study exposure–MIC relationships. Conclusion: individualized therapy considering bacterial susceptibility, drug exposure, and comorbidities, with TDM for selected patients, may improve outcomes and curb resistance.
notes: スウェーデンの学術機関からの博士論文。1992-2014年のスウェーデンにおける158例のMDR-TBコホート研究および中国での今後の研究計画について記載。MDR-TBは継続的な公衆衛生課題であるが、本記事は新規のアウトブレイクや急性イベントを報告するものではなく、治療最適化に関する学術研究である。

articleSummary: Streptococcus suis infection, presenting as meningitis and septicemia, continues in Thailand with 49 cases and 3 deaths as of 9 March 2026, linked to Ju-Soi Alley raw-larb enthusiasts. Rajavithi Hospital and the Department of Medical Services warn transmission occurs via consumption of raw or undercooked pork or pork blood, or contact with blood/meat from sick pigs through wounds or mucous membranes. Onset typically 3–5 days after exposure. Diagnosis relies on blood and CSF cultures; high-risk groups include the elderly and individuals with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or immunosuppression. Treatment starts with IV antibiotics covering likely pathogens, then targeted therapy after culture results; complications may include permanent deafness, endocarditis, arthritis, or brain abscess requiring neurosurgical consultation. Prevention emphasizes avoiding raw pork, using protective gear for handlers, diligent hand hygiene, and general health maintenance.

articleSummary: Mexico's Cofepris approved sanitary registration for Qdenga (TAK-003), a dengue vaccine developed by Mahidol University, Thailand, and Takeda. The vaccine uses attenuated dengue serotypes 1–4 and is the second WHO-approved dengue vaccine, recommended for use in areas with high transmission. Qdenga is already used in 41 countries and is deployed in Latin America in Argentina, Paraguay, Brazil, and Colombia. In dengue-endemic countries like Mexico, it is recommended for people with comorbidities even outside the standard age range. The two-dose schedule requires at least a three-month interval. Pricing ranges from roughly 40 to 115 USD per dose (about 711–2,049 MXN), with many Latin American countries providing it free in focal areas. The CMN previously denied the vaccine's registration in 2021.

articleSummary: Measles cases are rising ahead of Eid al-Fitr 2026 in Indonesia, with Sukoharjo district yet to report any infections. Data from the Ministry of Health through week 8 of 2026 show 10,453 suspected measles cases, 8,372 confirmed, and six deaths, plus 45 outbreaks across 29 districts in 11 provinces (North Sumatra, West Sumatra, South Sumatra, Banten, West Java, Central Java, Yogyakarta, East Java, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi, and Central Sulawesi). Sukoharjo’s Health Office reports no current cases; prevention is being intensified, including MR vaccination for 9-month-olds with a booster at 18 months and additional school-based immunization via posyandu and puskesmas. Public guidance emphasizes exclusive breastfeeding for six months, balanced nutrition, vitamin A, and hygiene (handwashing, covering coughs). Watch for fever, red rash, cough, runny nose, or red eyes; seek care promptly at a puskesmas or doctor. Masks are recommended to limit spread; early detection remains a priority.

articleHeadline: Viêm ruột do ngộ độc sau ăn bánh mì heo quay
articleSummary: As of 2026-03-09, in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, a 45-year-old woman developed chills, abdominal pain, and frequent diarrhea after eating a roast pork banh mi. Diagnosed with postprandial bacterial enteritis; her blood infection marker was 110 mg/L, about 20x the normal limit (<5 mg/L). Clinically: fever, rigors, severe abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea. The causative agent in the banh mi was not yet confirmed, but Salmonella infection is suspected. Salmonella is a gut bacterium transmitted via undercooked meats, eggs, dairy, and greens; incubation is 2-48 hours, with cramps, vomiting, fever, and diarrhea that can last 7-10 days. The patient was hospitalized, given IV fluids and antibiotics, and after 3 days improved enough to eat porridge and soup. Preventive guidance: practice food hygiene, wash hands, separate raw and cooked foods, refrigerate cooked dishes within two hours, and ensure thorough cooking. Yogurt with probiotics may aid gut recovery.

articleSummary: An adult case from Hanoi, Vietnam: a 32-year-old preschool teacher presented with high fever 39–40°C, vesicular rash, cough and dyspnea. CT chest showed bilateral lung involvement with ground-glass opacities and consolidations, diagnosed as varicella pneumonia with secondary bacterial infection. Labs showed leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and elevated CRP. Treated with systemic antiviral therapy plus IV antibiotics, fluids/electrolytes, pruritus relief, and skin care; after 4 days, fever subsided, cough diminished, and dyspnea resolved; lesions crusted, patient discharged with home isolation and outpatient care. Varicella-Zoster virus is transmitted via respiratory droplets or direct vesicle contact. In adults, infection can progress quickly and cause pneumonia, hepatic and neurologic complications if untreated. Vaccination is 90–95% effective and recommended for children and adults lacking immunity. Workers in crowded settings (teachers, healthcare workers) and women of childbearing potential are emphasized. Those with prior infection may still benefit from herpes zoster vaccination to reduce shingles risk and complications.

articleSummary: Influenza A(H3N2) drives a spike in influenza-like illness in Ceará, Brazil, with Greater Fortaleza concentrating most cases. Since January, Fortaleza has logged 7,616 influenza-like illness attendances at urgent care units, up 28.7% from the prior year (5,914). The Ceará State Health Secretariat notes potential geographic spread beyond the Região Metropolitana de Fortaleza. A potentially emergent subclade K of H3N2 (J.2.4.1) has been detected, with at least three Ceará cases in 2026 (two in Caucaia, one in Fortaleza). Of 11 samples analyzed in February, eight were H3N2 and three were subclade K. Subclade K arrived in Brazil in December; WHO alerts highlight higher transmission potential while not implying greater virulence; current vaccine remains protective. High-risk groups are the elderly, pregnant women, and children under 5 (especially under 2). In Fortaleza, cases are prominent among 20–29-year-olds and children ≤4 years. Síndrome gripal symptoms include fever, chills, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, and altered smell/taste; nasal obstruction in children; elderly may show non-respiratory signs such as confusion or drowsiness.

articleSummary: As of March 9, 2026, Sukoharjo Regency, Indonesia, has no reported measles cases, but the local Health Office (DKK) is intensifying immunization and urging residents to seek medical evaluation if symptoms appear. Measles is a highly contagious respiratory virus transmitted by coughs or sneezes; initial symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, and red eyes, followed by a rash that typically starts on the face and spreads to the body. Children remain the most vulnerable, especially if unvaccinated, though adults can be infected if not immune. His community-based approach helped establish the world’s first vector-control system for Chagas and he proposed eradicating the insect from the Southern Cone, a plan adopted by PAHO in 1991, aiding Argentina, Venezuela, Mexico and Panama. A tropical medicine specialist trained at USP and UFMG, he led the Center for Studies and Prophylaxis of Chagas Disease in Minas Gerais, later integrated into Fiocruz Minas. He created a blood-donor program and a state laboratory for diagnosing transfusion-transmitted diseases. He served on the WHO Expert Committee on Neglected Diseases, led the National Health Foundation in 1992, and received major Brazilian honors. He died December 31 at 87 from acute renal failure with heart failure and lymphoma, survived by his wife Rosinha and four children.

articleHeadline: New 2030 Global Targets for Histoplasmosis from International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) 2025 Histoplasmosis Working Group
articleSummary: Histoplasmosis is a neglected, life-threatening fungal infection disproportionately affecting people living with HIV/AIDS and other immunocompromised individuals in endemic regions. ISHAM formed a Histoplasmosis Working Group at its 2025 congress in Iguazu Falls, Brazil (May 20–24, 2025) to advance awareness, research, diagnostics and treatment, capacity building, and fungal biology. The group highlighted gaps and innovations—lateral flow and molecular diagnostics—and the need for biobanks and validated diagnostic algorithms. A global 90-90-90 target for symptomatic histoplasmosis by 2030 was proposed, modeled on UNAIDS. Regional history in Latin America and the Caribbean includes initiatives since 2013 (Manaus Declaration) that aimed for 80 by 2020 and 100 by 2025.

articleHeadline: From emergency to integration: research as the bridge in mpox control
articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) control shifts from emergency status to an integrated phase as of 9 March 2026, with research guiding policy on vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostics. In DR Congo, the MVA-BN two-dose primary series induces durable immune memory in health-care workers; a booster triggers rapid anamnestic responses and ~90-fold rise in neutralising antibodies by day 14, with day-545 titres six-fold above baseline, aligning with WHO guidance for routine mpox vaccination in endemic Africa. A prospective safety cohort of 1600 HCWs shows booster safety with no serious adverse events and comparable safety for liquid vs. lyophilised formulations. Uganda employed a single-dose strategy during vaccine shortages, though durability remains uncertain. No licensed mpox therapeutics exist; the Mpox Study in Africa aims to evaluate antivirals and management. Diagnostics remain bottlenecks: NG-Test sensitivity below WHO targets, especially in DR Congo; Uganda performs better but is variable. Rwanda’s mpox IgG ELISA enables serosurveillance, though correlates of protection are undefined.

articleSummary: As of March 9, 2026, rising measles cases in Indonesia are presented as an indicator of waning population immunity. Dr. Aisyah Amanda Hanif of IPB University notes that about 90% of non-immune people are at risk upon exposure, making high vaccination coverage critical. Herd immunity is achieved when more than 94% of the population are immune, via vaccination or prior infection; Indonesia's Ministry of Health targets at least 95% immunization coverage for measles. Measles is airborne, typically entering through the respiratory tract; after infection, the virus replicates and spreads to various organs, with the characteristic rash arising from the immune response.

articleSummary: Measles has been detected in at least 73 cities across Indonesia as of 2026-03-10, with cases rising. Initial symptoms resemble flu, followed by a high fever (>38°C) for about 4-7 days, plus cough, runny nose, red eyes (conjunctivitis) with light sensitivity, and often diarrhea. A red rash typically appears after several days, starting behind the ears and face and spreading to the body; it lasts around a week and may darken before peeling. Since January 2026, Europe has reported numerous imported cases, including about 20 infections acquired during Maldives visits. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, with vectors active at dawn and dusk and occasionally daytime in shaded areas; incubation is 3–14 days. Clinical presentation ranges from high fever, severe headache behind the eyes, myalgia/arthralgia, nausea, vomiting, and rash to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever or dengue shock syndrome. Four serotypes exist; prior infection with one does not protect against others and can raise severe disease risk after secondary infection. Vaccination with Qdenga (two doses, 3 months apart) and strict vector control are advised. Global Jan 2026 reports exceed 100,000 cases and over 10 deaths in 39 countries; additional at-risk areas include Indonesia (Bali, Lombok), Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nicaragua, Honduras, Madeira, and southern Europe.

articleSummary: Jakarta, Indonesia—The World Health Organization issued new tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis guidelines, endorsing near-point-of-care molecular testing to diagnose TB for the first time, alongside easily collected swab (saliva) testing to broaden access. A low-cost sputum-collection strategy is also recommended to improve testing efficiency for initial TB detection and rifampicin resistance. The guidelines aim to close persistent diagnostic gaps that leave millions with delayed or missed TB diagnoses, due to reliance on sputum samples not producible by all patients, limited lab availability, and high costs. The recommendations specify near-point-of-care testing for TB without rifampicin resistance at peripheral health facilities and communities; swab specimens used with NPOC; sputum-based testing using LC-NAAT to detect rifampicin resistance where resources permit. WHO urges rapid adoption to enable earlier TB diagnosis, per Dr. Tereza Kasaeva.

articleSummary: Lawyers on 9 March 2026 petition Bangkok Remand Prison and Rajthani Prison Hospital to transfer Amp Nawarat, a Section 112 detainee with preexisting HIV, for treatment after leg lesions raised concerns of monkeypox amid outbreak reports. articleSummary: In the first seven weeks of 2026, suspected dengue cases in Brazil’s Federal District fell 62.4% to 1,719 from 4,579 year-ago.
